---
title: "AI and Job Postings: From Destruction to Creation?"
description: "Indeed Hiring Lab finds the relationship between AI exposure and job-posting growth may be flipping, with the most AI-exposed occupations, led by software development, now rebounding fastest."
author: synesis
date: "2026-07-13"
image: cover.jpg
---

![Software developers at work. Image from [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

[Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/) reports a reversal: the occupations most exposed to AI, which fell hardest from 2022 to 2026, are now leading the rebound in job postings. US software-development postings are up almost 15% since [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) launched in late February 2025, while postings overall fell 7% over the same window.

What the report finds:

- **A software rebound off a low base.** Since Claude Code's late-February-2025 launch, the same month the term "vibecoding" was coined, US software-development postings on Indeed have risen almost 15%, while overall postings fell about 7%. But software still stands at index 72.5 (February 2020 = 100), about 27.5% below its pre-pandemic level, while overall postings are essentially flat at 101.4. The rebound is a change in slope well short of a recovery.

![US job postings indexed to February 2020. Software development has turned up over the past year but remains far below its 2021–22 peak and its pre-pandemic level. Chart from [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/).](chart-timeseries.png){fig-align="center"}

- **The rebound shows up across most rich economies.** The software-development share of all postings is climbing in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia, with Germany and France the exceptions. Hiring Lab notes that the English-speaking countries have the most consistent gains, and reads that as possible earlier adoption of agentic-AI tools.

![The software-development share of all postings across six economies. It is rising in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia, and still falling in Germany. Chart from [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/).](chart-international.png){fig-align="center"}

- **The AI-exposure relationship flipped.** From May 2022 to May 2026, the more of an occupation's skills generative AI could transform, the more its postings fell, a statistically significant if uncontrolled correlation, with declines that began before ChatGPT's late-2022 release. Over the most recent year the slope reverses: higher AI exposure now predicts a larger rebound, and not only for software development.

![Change in US postings from May 2022 to May 2026 against each occupation's GenAI exposure. The most exposed occupations, including software development, declined the most. Chart from [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/).](chart-exposure-decline.webp){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="chart-exposure-decline-full.png"}

![The same comparison for May 2025 to May 2026. The slope reverses: the most AI-exposed occupations, led by software development, now rebound the most. Chart from [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/).](chart-exposure-rebound.webp){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="chart-exposure-rebound-full.png"}

- **The gains are senior and AI-fluent.** 71% of the net rise in software-development postings from May 2025 to May 2026 came from senior roles (titles with senior, lead, principal, director, or manager) and 37% from titles mentioning AI (AI, machine learning, deep learning, or prompt). The two categories overlap. Hiring Lab reads this as demand for experienced people who can work with AI, consistent with prior evidence on AI's disproportionate hit to entry-level jobs.

![Share of the net rise in software-development postings from senior roles and from AI-titled roles, which overlap. Chart from [Indeed Hiring Lab](https://www.hiringlab.org/2026/07/08/ai-and-job-postings-from-destruction-to-creation/).](chart-decomposition.png){fig-align="center"}

- **Hiring Lab's read: destruction turning to creation.** It describes the shift as AI exposure moving from job destruction toward job creation, with AI mentions in titles now spreading beyond software into other white-collar occupations. The report stresses that correlation is not causation, treats the Claude Code timing as a coincidence it declines to over-read, and argues the future of work depends on how the exposure-versus-postings slope evolves.

## My Notes

- **The rebound favors AI-augmented senior roles.** The net gain is concentrated in senior and AI-titled work, so what looks like job creation is closer to AI augmenting experienced developers, the augment-over-replace case in [Daron Acemoglu on AI, Jobs, and Liberal Democracy](/posts/20260524-acemoglu-great-displacement/), than to genuinely new demand for software.

- **Entry-level hiring keeps shrinking.** The net gain is in senior roles, while payroll data shows early-career software developers still contracting: [The AI Entry-Level Jobs Effect Isn't Fading](/posts/20260628-ai-entry-level-jobs/) put workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed jobs down about 3.8% a year.

- **The same exposure metric now predicts rebounds.** Indeed's GenAI-exposure score marked the occupations that fell most through 2026 and now marks those rebounding most: exposure flags which occupations swing hardest, in either direction. The direction depends on the tool era and flipped when agentic tools arrived, a caution against treating any exposure measure, including the one in [GPTs Are GPTs: Labor Market Impact of Large Language Models](/posts/20230321-gpts-are-gpts-labor-market-impact/), as a one-way forecast.
